描述_EN: then, the colourful enamels were painted onto the surface and the whole piece was re-fired to the lower firing temperature of the enamels. as colourful glazes became more popular, potters were limited by the fact that many glazes ran together during firing, blurring their design. around 1200, at various kilns, potters began to initially cover the body with a transparent glaze and fire it to the very high temperatures required for the clay to harden fully. prior to the 13th century, chinese potters created their wares by forming the body of the piece, glazing and then firing it in a kiln. the result of this experiment was to evolve into the elaborate and colourful 'overglaze enamel' designs of later centuries. this bowl is a good example of one of the crucial innovations of the jin dynasty (1115-1234). the history of chinese ceramics is a fascinating story of innovation and discovery.
描述_ZN: 然后，彩色的珐琅彩被涂在表面，整个作品被重新烧到珐琅彩的较低烧制温度。 随着彩色釉料的流行，陶工们受到了限制，因为许多釉料在烧制过程中会跑到一起，模糊了他们的设计。 在1200年左右，在不同的窑场，陶工们开始最初用透明的釉料覆盖器身，并将其烧至粘土完全硬化所需的极高温度。 在13世纪之前，中国的陶艺家通过形成作品的主体，上釉，然后在窑中烧制来创造他们的作品。 这个实验的结果就是演变成了后来几个世纪的精心设计和色彩斑斓的 "釉上彩 "设计。 这个碗是金代（1115-1234）关键创新之一的一个好例子。 中国陶瓷的历史是一个迷人的创新和发现的故事。
